name: bash
description: Run a shell command on a host: the remote twin of the local Bash tool. stdout and stderr come back merged, in order; a non-zero exit adds an [exit code: N] line. Working directory: pass `cwd`, or pass the same `session` name on every call to make `cd` persist between calls; with neither, each call starts in the home directory. Output over ~100 KB is cut in the middle and kept in full in a file on the host (read it with `read`). Use run_in_background for long jobs, then ssh_job.

timeout.description: Milliseconds before the command is killed (default 120000, max 1800000)

cwd.description: Directory to run in: absolute, or relative to the session directory

session.description: Any name; calls that share it share a working directory that `cd` changes. Use one per conversation

run_in_background.description: Start it as a background job and return a jobId at once

description.description: What the command does (for the transcript; not used by the server)

name: bridge
description: Open a direct path from your own sandbox shell to this server, so files and command output move at network speed without passing through the model. Returns a time-limited URL and a one-line installer for the `box` command (exec, put, get, push, pull, call). Use it for bulk transfers, whole directories, binaries, and scripted sequences of commands.

ttl_hours.description: How long the URL stays valid

name: edit
description: Replace exact text in files on a host: the remote twin of the local Edit tool, and bulk-capable. old_string must match exactly and be unique in the file unless replace_all is set. Pass file_path/old_string/new_string for one edit, or `edits` for up to 50 edits across files in one call: edits to the same file apply in order, and a file is written only if all of its edits succeed.

file_path.description: Absolute path of the file to change

new_string.description: Text to put in its place

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

name: read
description: Read files on a host: the remote twin of the local Read tool, and bulk-capable. Text comes back as numbered lines (cat -n style); use offset/limit for long files. Images (png, jpg, gif, webp) come back as images. Pass file_path for one file, or `files` for up to 20 files read in one call.

file_path.description: Absolute path of the file to read

files.description: Several files in one call; they share the output budget

name: write
description: Create or overwrite files on a host: the remote twin of the local Write tool, and bulk-capable. Pass file_path + content for one file, or `files` for up to 50 files written in parallel in one call. Parent directories are created; an existing file keeps its mode and owner. For large or binary files use the bridge instead.

file_path.description: Absolute path of the file to write

content.description: Full new content of the file
